“question of deep ‘economic and political significance.’ ” The Court 
proceeded to hold that the term “estabhshed by the state” should be read 
to include “or estabhshed for a state by the federal government”—^thus 
effectively agreeing with the IRS’s interpretation of the statute. King v, 
Burwell thus had the effect of declaring that the IRS’s interpretation was 
correct, rather than simply permissible, which in turn meant that no future 
IRS could amend the rule to adopt a contrary, but perhaps also permissible, 
interpretation.
Mead, Brand A, and King v, Burwell were by no means the Court’s 
only important pronouncements about the scope of the Chevron doctrine. 
For instance, in City of Arlington v. FCC, 569 U.S. 290 (2013), the Court 
held that Chevron applied to agency interpretations of their own 
jurisdiction or authority.
Leaving to one side their precise holdings, taken together, these cases 
demonstrate how the ^^Chevron doctrine” ebbed and fiowed in the decades 
foUowing the Court’s decision. The Court adopted several different 
perspectives on parceling out deference to agency legal interpretation.
Over time, however. Chevron became the target of increased criticism, 
both at the Court and beyond. Between the years 2016 and 2024, the Court 
did not defer to an agency interpretation under Chevron. Some members of 
the Court lodged criticisms of its premises. See, e.g,, Pereira v. Sessions, 
585 U.S. 198, 219-21 (Kennedy, J., concurring); Michigan v. EPA, 576 U.S. 
743, 760-64 (2015) (Thomas, J., concurring); Buffington v. McDonough, 598 
U.S. ----, 143 S. Ct. 14, 19—20 (Gorsuch, J., dissenting from denial of
certiorari); Brett M. Kavanaugh, Fixing Statutory Interpretation, 129 
Ha r v . L. Re v . 2119, 2150—54 (2016). During approximately that same time 
period. Congress considered, but did not enact, proposed legislation that 
would have abolished Chevron deference. See, e.g., S. 909, 116th Cong., 1st 
Sess., § 2 (2019); H. R. 5, 115th Cong., 1st Sess., § 202 (2017).
This sequence of events led to the litigation that upended the formal 
Chevron framework, which featured both criticisms and defenses of the 
doctrine.
